decisions.reason: On Borel [0,1] with Lebesgue probability, let A be a non-Borel subset of a Borel null Cantor set N and F the uniform [2,3] CDF. The diagonal perturbation G_n(x)(omega)=F(x)+1{omega in A and x=omega} has measurable fixed-x evaluations and CDF paths outside N, with pointwise convergence in probability, but its raw supremum error is the nonmeasurable 1_A. The conclusion was undefined. Repaired by specifying everywhere-CDF paths and a measurable-null-set replacement convention, retaining the almost-sure input case through versions.

On Borel [0,1] with Lebesgue probability, take non-Borel A inside a Borel null Cantor set, X=3/2, F its point-mass CDF, and Ghat(x)(omega)=F(x)+1{omega in A and x=omega}. Every fixed-x evaluation is measurable and the paths are CDFs outside the null set. With epsilon=2 and delta=0 the error hypothesis is the whole space, but q_Ghat(1/2) equals omega on A and 3/2 otherwise. For alpha_1=0 and alpha_2=1/2, coverage is the nonmeasurable complement of A. Repaired with everywhere-CDF versions and explicit exceptional-set handling before any quantile, supremum or probability is formed.

Continuity is required only of F; neither completeness, independence nor additional choice is used. This is repair verification, not independent review of the repair.

Null-set replacement preserves measurable evaluations; everywhere-CDF paths make the rational quantile identity and rational supremum identity hold pointwise. Measurability is established before the trivial-bound branch. In the nontrivial branch all shifted levels lie in (0,1); deterministic tail inclusions and a union bound prove coverage without independence. Parts 1 and 2 and all numerical constants remain unchanged. This verifies the repair without claiming independent review.
